# Branching on a one-shot run's outcome without parsing output

`rimsky compose run` reports three outcome classes on its exit status. A
surrounding script branches on `$?` alone and never reads the transcript.

## The three classes

| exit | class |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | all succeeded |
| 1 | something failed |
| 2 | the run was bounded out |

## All succeeded

```yaml
project: outcome-success
templates:
  - path: ./template-success.yml
instances:
  - template: pass
  - template: pass
```

```bash
rimsky compose run rimsky-compose-all-success.yml >/dev/null 2>&1
echo $?   # 0
```

## Something failed

```yaml
project: outcome-failure
templates:
  - path: ./template-success.yml
  - path: ./template-failure.yml
instances:
  - template: pass
  - template: fail
```

```bash
rimsky compose run rimsky-compose-one-failure.yml >/dev/null 2>&1
echo $?   # 1
```

A script tells a run that produced a real failure from one that did not, and
fails rather than proceeding, without inspecting any output.

## Bounded out

```yaml
project: outcome-bounded
templates:
  - path: ./template-slow.yml
instances:
  - template: slow
```

`template-slow.yml` fetches an upstream that sleeps for 20 seconds.

```bash
rimsky compose run --timeout 3s rimsky-compose-slow.yml >/dev/null 2>&1
echo $?   # 2
```

Distinct from both success and failure. A script escalates a run that ran out of
time rather than treating it as a failed check.

## The branch

```bash
rimsky compose run "$MANIFEST" >/dev/null 2>&1
case $? in
  0) echo all-succeeded ;;
  1) echo something-failed ;;
  2) echo bounded-out ;;
esac
```

No two classes share a status, which is what makes them branchable at all.
